en: When Mayon Volcano shows a lava dome, people must stay outside its six-kilometer Permanent Danger Zone to avoid deadly rockfalls.
During heavy typhoons in Benguet province, stay away from steep slopes because saturated soil causes deadly landslides.
The Cagayan River swells rapidly during monsoons, so never cross its muddy waters to avoid dangerous flash floods.
In the arid plains of Ilocos Norte, wear hats and drink water during summer to prevent heatstroke from intense sun exposure.
After floods in Manila, avoid wading in contaminated water to prevent leptospirosis, a severe bacterial infection spread by rat urine.
When hiking Mount Pulag in Benguet, wear thick jackets because temperatures drop below freezing at its summit, risking hypothermia.
Swim only in lifeguarded beaches in Palawan, as strong rip currents in the West Philippine Sea can pull swimmers underwater.
Protect the forests of the Sierra Madre because their trees filter air pollutants, ensuring cleaner breathing air for nearby communities.
Avoid swimming in Laguna de Bay during algal blooms, as toxic cyanobacteria can cause severe skin rashes and stomach illnesses.
If you feel a strong earthquake in coastal Davao, immediately evacuate to higher ground to escape potential deadly tsunamis.
Apply sunscreen when visiting Tagaytay, because higher altitudes near Taal Volcano expose your skin to stronger, sunburn-causing ultraviolet radiation.
During the rainy season in Quezon City, empty stagnant water in tires to eliminate mosquito breeding sites and prevent dengue fever.
